text:
A: Hiya! Hello, I'm Gemma.
B: Neil. Hello.
A: Hi Neil. Where are you calling from?
B: Halifax.
A: Oh, nice. I'm Taunton, down in Somerset. What do you do, then?
B: Stonemason. Restoration, mostly. Churches, chapels, old mills.
A: Oh wow, that's not one you hear every day. Like carving and that?
B: Some carving, when I'm lucky. A lot of it's repair. Taking out stone that's failed and putting new in, and repointing. Last week I was taking out someone else's cement pointing on a chapel in Hebden Bridge. Somebody'd done the whole gable in hard cement maybe thirty year ago, and it traps the water in, so the stone does the breaking instead of the mortar. Faces just come off in sheets. It should've been lime. It's always lime on a building that age. Folk think cement's stronger, so it must be better, and it's not. It's vandalism, frankly.
A: Vandalism! Strong words.
B: It's true, though.
A: No, I believe you. It's like when people put the wrong dressing on a wound because it looks sturdier, and it just keeps all the gunk in. I'm a nurse, sorry, that's the only thing I've got to compare it to.
B: Nah, that's fair, actually. Same principle. It's got to breathe.
A: It's got to breathe. There you go. We're basically in the same trade.
B: I wouldn't go that far.
A: Ha, fair. Erm, so what do you do when you're not doing stone?
B: Walk. Swim, outdoors. I was in Gaddings Dam on Sunday.
A: Outside? In this weather?
B: It's not that bad once you're in. The first minute's awful. After that you stop thinking about owt else.
A: That's the bit I'd never get past, the first minute. I do parkrun, that's my limit. Vivary Park on a Saturday. I'm not fast, I'm just sort of there.
B: That's most of it. Turning up.
A: Do you watch any sport? Liam, my partner, has got me into the rugby.
B: Rugby league. Halifax Panthers.
A: Oh, is that different? We watch Bath sometimes, and the Six Nations.
B: That's union. Different game.
A: Is it very different? Sorry, I genuinely don't know.
B: Thirteen players, not fifteen. Fewer stoppages. Er, less standing about in heaps. I'm biased.
A: Less standing about in heaps, that's a selling point. I'll tell Liam, he'll be livid. I mostly go for the pub after anyway, to be honest.
B: Can't argue with that bit.
A: Did you always want to do stone, then? Like, from school?
B: Er. Not exactly. I was good at art. Teacher wanted me to go to art college. I did an apprenticeship instead, because it paid. I sometimes think about it.
A: About the art college?
B: Yeah. Then I carve a bit of tracery for a church window and I think, well, this is drawing, just slower.
A: That's actually really lovely, drawing, just slower. Do you still sketch, then, like on—
